allowed_result_differences.before: FIRST MEASUREMENT of Decisio 0.9.0 on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B in this intake (submitted through the form). A NEW ROW of the Decisio family, with a different base from the live Gemma-based Decisio rows; it replaces none of them. 'Jev-compatible' describes the interface only. SERVED WEIGHTS: base_model Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (served: Qwen's official FP8 release at 95a723d0). These are the official Qwen FP8 weights, not a Decisio fine-tune; the server is aminry/decisio v0.9.0, run as frozen in code_revision. SIBLING CHECK: none of the 42 weight-shard LFS hashes equals an LFS blob of the 173 live row repositories in the pre-launch snapshot (171 checked; Uniphore/uniphore-4b-decider and nemotron-deciffusion/Nemotron-Deciffusion-8B-v2 returned 401 and were unchecked). This compares bytes at repository HEAD, not each published row's revision, and is not a claim of independent training. PROMPT AND READOUT: one user turn with state, instructions and lettered options, Qwen chat template with thinking disabled, and an Answer: prefill; up to 1,055 leading newline tokens pad the state prefix to the hybrid's 1,056-token block. No system turn. Yes/no is presented as A. No and B. Yes, with any side descriptions retained, and the returned probabilities are keyed back to yes/no. Choice defaults hide index-like keys, describe options and desnake bare labels; these are item-blind label-shape rules, never answer-key changes. Score levels are lettered options. One label-logprob readout per question, max_tokens 1, no generated explanation; softmax probabilities are temperature-scaled at 1.370 for choice and 1.506 for yes/no and score, preserving argmax. No commit rule, no task-specific calibration or abstention, no ensemble and no retry. TEMPERATURE FIT (author statement): the source describes fitting on the author's private 1,400-item suite; the examples were not inspected and overlap with JevBench was not independently checked. Base-model training contamination of the sealed draw is unchecked. PREFIX CACHE: standard vLLM automatic prefix caching is on, with Mamba align mode; repeated padded state prefixes can reuse KV/GDN state across requests. Its floating-point effect is part of the served configuration; the replay also reads the cache. SPECULATIVE DECODING/MTP OFF, despite the shipped MTP weights. CONTEXT AND REFUSALS: the frozen tag has no dedicated over-limit refusal handler and no truncation. An engine prompt of 32,767 tokens is accepted; 32,768 or more triggers vLLM's context-length validation exception, which this tag leaves as bare HTTP 500 'Internal Server Error'. Exactly the 15 preregistered over-length items returned that bare 500 with the required context-error log evidence and are scored as misses, without retry or partial credit. The other 1,485 items returned HTTP 200; total 1,500 rows. Native outcome deviations are record-only under the preregistered amendment, never a reason to retry or improve a score: measured outcome deviations 0. The wrapper's remaining post-sealed stops concern infrastructure/configuration and the frozen driver's own unchanged stop rule. USAGE AND BILLING: server-reported 664,205 input and 1,485 output tokens; 0 usage mismatches against the offline count. Input usage counts state and question text without padding or template; the billed input is instead the preregistered engine-prompt transcription, 1,761,623, as detailed in cost_basis. A server-observed engine count was unavailable under the frozen configuration, so the native usage agreement is not an independent validation of the engine total. The earlier preregistration estimate near 1.13x the cap used a rough usage basis and is superseded by engine-basis billing, 2.77x the cap on the common basis. HARDWARE AND LATENCY: one RTX PRO 6000 96 GB, so these measurements do not establish latency on any other card or hosted service. Measured loopback p95 about 0.07 s, maximum about 0.13 s, 0 requests over 10 s; scored loop 91 s. No decision receives a time-limit miss in the v1.7 share view on these timings. That view uses the common self-hosted latency estimate (2 times measured p50 plus 0.15 s), an assumption about hosted latency rather than a hosted-endpoint measurement. DETERMINISM (record-only): first 50 requests replayed twice after scoring, 50/50 bit-identical, 0 argmax flips, maximum probability difference 0.0. The scored run stands. PREREGISTRATION: append-only amendments before any pod froze MTP off and both input totals, changed native outcome deviations to record-only, and selected engine-input billing with an explicit offline-transcription limitation. The earlier suggestion that extra head-recompute requests should enlarge this run's engine basis was corrected: with empty tasks and debug off they do not occur on the frozen route, and no phantom tokens are billed. ATTEMPT HISTORY: create calls 1-5 failed with Verda HTTP 503 before an instance existed (absence receipts retained). Call 6 was the sole measured attempt; zero sealed items reached a model before it. LICENCE: Decisio server Apache-2.0 with NOTICE; Qwen weights Apache-2.0, ungated.

NATIVE OUTPUTS: next-token probabilities over the option codes, choice argmax and probabilities, noul P(true), score expectation and probabilities; the first-party transport shim adds no prompt text or probability arithmetic. AUTHOR EXPOSURE: the preregistration records training data as undisclosed (Decision Index note) and author-reported Decision Index suite figures; no overlap or contamination audit was run by us. Maximum 44.157234 s, median 0.122518 s, p95 0.358708 s. DETERMINISM: first 50 positions run twice, 50/50 bit-identical, 0 argmax flips, maximum probability difference 0.0. ATTEMPT HISTORY: attempt 1, pod window 24 Oct 2026 05:52-06:21Z (about USD 1.24) on a separate disposable GPU instance, stopped the 31b row after 1,057 of 1,500 items at the runner's own time cap. Amendment 3 corrected the first-party runner to use cold nonce-bearing probes, maximum anchor latency and a long-item budget floor; a further review preceded the retry. evaluator exposure and device ruling admitted the fresh full 31b run as the final same-use retry; 4b remained a first use. Attempt 2 is this measurement, both rows back to back on new a separate disposable GPU instance, 24 Oct 07:59-08:36Z, about USD 1.57 rental. OVER COST CAP: measured USD 0.080894606 per 1,000 decisions on the common basis = 1.252342099x; ranked_over_cap, uncapped views only (ruling on file).

allowed_result_differences.before: THE AUTHORS' OWN SERVER, run unmodified: PelaAI/KnowLine-31B-Gen1 at 986803e4037f7778d24623184729a31202e3d302, knowline_server.py sha256 13ca50c4001fac0aa3899a35ff01e60f311132c571b17a8c3dc7aa6001ad2f3f (1,156 lines) and knowline_layout.py sha256 2e839fa24f1ad9c980898b2a9aa62e2154ba3f57618bd5f2fedb5756f61f062f (242 lines), plus the data file temperatures.json sha256 463a46c5ea253649bd5f43809655637d2d41939e503c81ddd01b28355d736f62 ({"score": 0.6944}), all mounted read-only at /model over stock SGLang 0.5.21. Only these two author Python files shipped; knowline_engine.py and serve_knowline.sh were excluded and never executed (the SGLang flags follow the author's serve_knowline.sh, plus our one pooling flag --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.15, see below). Commands: env HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /model --served-model-name m --tp 1 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --enable-fp32-lm-head --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.15 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9080 ; env HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 /model/knowline_server.py --model /model --backend sglang --url http://127.0.0.1:9080 --served-model-name knowline-31b-gen1 --temperature 1 --workers 16 --read-twice --twice-max-tokens 3000 --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --temperatures /model/temperatures.json --box-prompt gemma --box-coords yxyx. Never passed: --allow-url-assets, --referenced-fields, --header, --no-read-twice, --debug-refusals, --box-calibration, --box-prompt-template (asserted on the rendered launch script; /health after the measurement shows referenced_fields false, url_assets false, no box calibration). Image: lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.21-cu130@sha256:b1259f3ea3275f66237c498ea388919729018bc9f01c3d638391e06e2cf3f469, derived image sha256:579dd709d9118e745c9be62fc134fc6aac272a2ee75834da15f7cd235a025a4e (only blank-credential ENV, no package installs). Python 3.12.3, sglang 0.5.21, torch 2.13.0+cu130, transformers 5.12.1, tokenizers 0.22.2, flashinfer-python 0.6.18, sglang-kernel 0.4.7. Code gate: cleared by the benchmark owner on the disclosed patterns. DISCLOSED PATTERNS: a new dormant runtime download path, requests.get of http(s) image URLs (knowline_server.py _fetch, line 383), reachable only behind the command-line flag --allow-url-assets (off by default, never passed, container without network); dormant Hub-capable from_pretrained loaders in the unused --backend hf class; served tokenizer load from local /model under offline flags; HTTP client exclusively to loopback SGLang /generate (scoring and the dormant box path); local listening socket on 127.0.0.1. About 800 added lines (image, box and referenced-fields code) are not reachable from text-only requests; the one text-path change (noul criteria values rendered through render_value) leaves string, null and number criteria byte-identical and is mirrored by our offline token counter. Delta source review PASS WITH CONDITIONS (flag discipline, hash-checked snapshot, in-container offline proof, all enforced by the runner), the runner was reviewed and findings fixed. OUR ONE LAUNCH-FLAG CHANGE (pre-registration Amendment 3): attempt 1 stopped in the synthetic smoke because the default SGLang pool sizing (--swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.8) gave only 29,717 full-attention cache tokens; attempt 2 adds --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.15, which only reallocates the same KV memory between the full-attention and sliding-window pools (live capacity max_total_num_tokens 106,983, max_req_input_len 106,977); no change to weights, BF16 precision, KV dtype, mem-fraction, context configuration or the 1,024-token attention window; bit identity against the default sizing is not promised. The amendment was reviewed and the final hashes checked (final runner sha256 18c051f1b72ec682339a11eb90025eb4c73fc4b526932c24f3faecf557fc270d), covered by the standing clearance for this amendment. Weights: Apache-2.0, public, ungated, 62,546,336,352 weight bytes in 13 BF16 shards, hash-checked file by file on the node; prereg manifest sha256 0444b046991995634646ef018d16103292eb9807147d0287898b2380b95ed98d; the shards share no LFS sha256 with the weights of the measured KnowLine 4B, 26B and 35B rows. FIRST MEASUREMENT of KnowLine-31B-Gen1 (our own intake). FIRST DENSE-GEMMA KnowLine: new weights (Gemma 4 31B-it fine-tune, LoRA rank 32 merged, then averaged 0.75 fine-tuned + 0.25 base per tensor, readout temperature 1.44 folded into the final norm and soft-cap), not a new serving version of an earlier row; the 4B, 26B and 35B KnowLine rows are different weights. AUTHOR'S OWN SERVER on our rented hardware, bf16 (no FP8; the author documents bf16 only). The server and layout files are not the bytes measured for the earlier KnowLine rows (1,156 lines against 367; see code_revision); on our text items the prompts follow the same read-twice layout. NATIVE OUTPUTS: label-token logprobs, label-only softmax at temperature 1 for choice and noul questions and at the author's 0.6944 for score questions (temperatures.json, effective 1.0 on top of the folded 1.44; both are ranking-relevant behaviours of the author's server); choice argmax, Noul P(true), score expectation; header off, no rotation, no calibration file. AUTHOR EXPOSURE (card, self-reported, not verified): Decision Index 0.3 public suite 70.13, self-run read twice; the card also reports JevBench / JevBench-hard evaluations; the training data is that of KnowLine-26B-A4B-Gen1 (906,122 rows, about 33% targeting Decision Index benchmarks in their request format, including train splits of public datasets rewritten in that format and synthetic items in the same format); the authors checked it against the Decision Index 0.3 rows, their own evaluation sets and public benchmarks including JevBench and removed 491 near-duplicate rows; the 0.75 averaging weight was chosen on the authors' own evaluation sets; LLM teachers labelled the synthetic tasks and not all labels were checked by a human; the card says part of the public-suite score comes from benchmarks whose tasks are in the training data. The authors say no Jev or other decision-model outputs were used as training labels. No overlap or contamination audit was run by us. The author's H20 timing (340 ms median, 3,977 ms at the 95th percentile) does not transfer to this RTX PRO 6000 measurement.
